title: HECATE: Path to Truly Self-Driving Networks
subtitle: Machine learning to optimize network flows in real time

achievement: Researchers presented a new method for improving network traffic management for software-defined networking tools, Hecate and PolKA.
By analyzing real-time traffic data, Hecate calculates the best paths for data while PolKA directs the traffic.
Researchers demonstrated practical solutions for efficient, self-managing networks and control flows in real time.
impact: Development of a truly self-driving network, which can make optimized decisions for science traffic on the network.
Researchers reduced latency, increased throughput, and tackled complex user demands for the necessary flow quality of experience.
Results show the latency to switch paths is minimal for real-time decision processing, previously never demonstrated in real infrastructure.
approach: Researchers proposed a novel framework that integrates PolKA with Hecate AI/ML optimization tool.
Dynamic switching and routing among multiple flow paths for autonomous, optimized routing decisions.

notes.presentation: TALKING POINTS:  ORNL researchers developed a new approach to enhance network traffic management using their tools Hecate and PolKA, which analyze real-time data to find optimal data paths and manage traffic for more efficient and self-regulating networks. These findings lay the groundwork for creating fully self-driving networks that can make real-time, optimized decisions for scientific data traffic, significantly reducing delays and improving performance, which has not been achieved in existing infrastructures before.  Researchers have proposed a new framework that combines the PolKA source routing tool with the Hecate AI/ML optimization tool, introducing new machine learning features and dynamic switching to enable initial autonomous routing decisions for improved network efficiency.
